summary: carbon.compute adds a provider-neutral compute layer and a RunPod adapter, tested only against a mock transport; no live RunPod call has been made from it. Provisioning persists an intent with a Carbon-generated ownership tag before any provider request and marks it as possibly sent before sending, so a lost create response is resolved by adopting the tagged pod, never by resending. Provision is idempotent per campaign and intent. Only a store-issued Carbon-owned resource can be stopped or terminated; a user-managed host has no such capability and an untagged or retagged pod is refused. A first provision requires a recorded account-balance observation, which is the spending cap, with the miner's own budget applied beneath it. The reconciler (python -m carbon.compute reconcile) runs from the controller host's store and the provider API alone, refuses to run on a rented pod, terminates Carbon-owned resources past deadline or campaign stop, and reports but never touches orphans or untagged pods. Estimates, provider-reported charges and unresolved charges stay separate, and storage that survives a stop is estimated. Concurrency admission is derived from observed host facts. The adapter issues only pod-lifecycle, balance and price requests. The stop and billing request shapes are not yet verified live. No scientific, security or production qualification is claimed.
